description.en: Learn to mock external dependencies, use monkeypatch for isolated tests, organize with conftest.py, and extend pytest with plugins.
description.ta: வெளிப்புற dependencies-ஐ mock செய்யவும், monkeypatch-உடன் isolated சோதனைகள் எழுதவும், conftest.py-உடன் ஒழுங்கமைக்கவும், plugins-உடன் pytest-ஐ விரிவாக்கவும் கற்றுக்கொள்ளுங்கள்.

story_variants.en:
## Vaathiyaar's Stunt Double

Vaathiyaar shows a movie poster. "In films, the hero doesn't jump off buildings — a stunt double does. In testing, when your code calls an API, database, or file system, you don't call the real thing. You use a **mock** — a stunt double for your dependencies."

### Mocking with unittest.mock
- `Mock()` — creates a fake object that records calls
- `patch()` — replaces a real object with a mock temporarily
- `MagicMock()` — Mock with magic methods pre-configured
- `mock.return_value` — set what the mock returns

### monkeypatch: pytest's Way
- `monkeypatch.setattr()` — replace attributes/functions
- `monkeypatch.setenv()` — set environment variables
- `monkeypatch.delenv()` — remove environment variables
- Automatically reverted after each test

### conftest.py
- Shared fixtures live in `conftest.py`
- No import needed — pytest discovers it automatically
- Can exist at multiple directory levels

> **Key Concept:** Never let tests depend on external systems. Mock the boundary, test the logic. Your tests should pass even on an airplane with no internet.

explanation.en: Our code uses requests to call an external API
Define a function that depends on an external API
Function that fetches weather data from an API
Makes an HTTP GET request — we do NOT want this in tests
Extract and return the temperature value
Now let's mock the API call in our test
Import patch (to replace) and MagicMock (fake object)
Write a test that mocks the API call
Replace requests.get with a mock during this test only
The mock is injected as a parameter to the test function
Configure: when .json() is called, return our fake data
Call the function — it uses the mock instead of real HTTP
Verify the function correctly extracted temperature from response
Verify the mock was called with the correct URL

left.label: Without Mock (BAD)
left.content:
def test_weather():
    # REAL API call!
    # Slow, flaky, needs internet
    result = get_weather('Chennai')
    assert result > 0  # brittle

instruction.en: Write a function `fetch_user(user_id)` that calls `requests.get()`. Then write a test using `@patch` that mocks the API and asserts the function returns the correct username from the mocked response.
instruction.ta: `requests.get()` அழைக்கும் `fetch_user(user_id)` செயல்பாடு எழுதுங்கள். பிறகு `@patch` பயன்படுத்தி API-ஐ mock செய்து சரியான username திருப்பப்படுகிறதா என்று assert செய்யும் test எழுதுங்கள்.

q.en: What does @patch do in a test?

en: Temporarily replaces an object with a mock
Patches a bug in the code
Sharing fixtures across test files without importing
ta: import செய்யாமல் test files-க்கிடையே fixtures-ஐ பகிர

en: Temporarily replaces an attribute, reverted after test
ta: ஒரு attribute-ஐ தற்காலிகமாக மாற்றும், சோதனைக்குப் பிறகு மீட்டமைக்கும்

under_the_hood.summary: patch and monkeypatch temporarily replace an attribute on a real module or object with a stand-in, and restore the original afterwards; a Mock records every call so the test can check how it was used.

steps.title: Names are looked up at call time
steps.body: If weather.py does `import requests` and later calls requests.get(url), Python looks up the attribute get on the requests module each time the line runs. Replace that attribute before the call and your code will call the replacement without knowing it. All mocking rests on this.

stages.label: patched?
stages.detail: finds the Mock instead of the real function

steps.title: Patch where it is used
steps.body: With `from requests import get` in weather.py, the name get is copied into the weather module. Patching requests.get then changes nothing for weather.py; you must patch 'weather.get'. The rule is: patch the name in the namespace where the code under test looks it up.

left.label: Wrong target
left.code:
# weather.py: from requests import get
patch('requests.get')
# weather.get still the real one

right.label: Right target
right.code:
patch('weather.get')
# the name weather.py actually uses

steps.title: A Mock invents attributes and records calls
steps.body: Mock() creates any attribute you touch on the fly, and calling it returns mock.return_value. Every call is recorded: mock.call_count, mock.call_args and mock_calls. So after the test you can assert mock_get.assert_called_once_with('https://api.example.com/temp').

steps.title: Restoring is the important half
steps.body: patch used as a decorator or with-block saves the original attribute and puts it back on exit. monkeypatch.setattr does the same, recording each change and undoing it at fixture teardown, in reverse order. Without the undo, one test's fake would leak into every test that runs after it.

steps.title: conftest.py shares fixtures
steps.body: pytest automatically loads conftest.py files in the test folders and their parents, and every fixture defined there is available to tests in that directory tree without importing it. A shared fake_api fixture in tests/conftest.py can then be used by every test file.

under_the_hood.takeaway: Mocking is attribute replacement plus call recording plus guaranteed restore. Patch the name where your code looks it up, and assert on how the fake was called.
